answer: A concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a stake-weighted reputation system. Every agent must lock real collateral before transacting, and each action it takes is carved into a public record like names on a stone ledge beside an atlas of all participants. Spawning fake identities then costs real stake per clone, so a sybil flood drains the attacker instead of the network. Honest workers rise through the atlas slowly and earn trusted partnerships that feel like a velvet glove, while duplicate accounts collapse under their own cost.
